title: PRism review benchmark · pilot
scope_note: Pilot corpus: two authored cases. Results are directional and not product-wide performance claims.
notes: Both updated PRism runs used the configured gemini-3.8-flash primary with gemini-3.1-flash-lite fallback; latency is one local run and includes model/API response time. The unstructured Gemini baseline is historical.

Human timed review is not measured yet. Defect precision/recall exclude non-defect metadata claims. The updated prompt no longer emits the unsupported coverage-unknown claim present in the earlier PRism run.
Updated PRism correctly cited the discount defect at src/discount.py:4. The unstructured response cited src/discount.py:1, so its defect detection was correct but its citation was not.

Added an authored timer-reconfiguration regression case. The first run missed it; after adding an explicit setting-change/in-flight-work trace and a citation anchor for the changed setting assignment, the reviewer detected it and cited src/mover.js:24 in 9.36 seconds.

The connected human-simulator#2 demo still has no supported defect: its setResumeAfterMs implementation clears and replaces the timer while the mover is running and yielded. Copilot's remaining suggestions are test/documentation advice rather than confirmed runtime bugs.

cases.spec: Reject discount rates below 0 or above 1.

gold.description: The implementation does not validate the stated 0..1 rate bounds, so out-of-range rates produce invalid discounts.

unstructured_gemini.adjudication: Detected the defect, but cited the function declaration instead of the faulty return line (line 4).

prism_gemini.adjudication: Detected and correctly cited the defect; returned one citation and no unsupported coverage status finding.

cases.spec: When the resume delay changes while the mover is paused for user input, replace the already-armed resume timer so the new delay takes effect immediately.

gold.description: Changing resumeAfterMs leaves the old timeout armed, so the mover resumes on the previous delay instead of the newly selected delay.

prism_gemini.adjudication: After prompting an explicit before/change/completion trace and anchoring citations to the changed setting assignment, PRism detected and correctly cited the stale active timer regression.
